extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and mentors for NIH K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Career Development Awards; NIH peer reviewers and grants administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Official peer-review criteria and committee guidance used to evaluate K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award applications, including the elements reviewers score and administrative determinations (human subjects, animals, biosafety, resource sharing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact/Priority score is assigned to reflect the reviewers' assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. For details see http://grants.nih.gov/grants/peer_review_process.htm#scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant as a candidate for the K08 award (training, prior research experience, publication record, and preparedness to undertake the proposed career development and research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate strengths such as advanced degrees (e.g., MD-PhD), focused prior training in the field, publication record (number and authorship), and prior productivity. Weaknesses (if any) are noted. Example strengths in this application: 'Very strong candidate with excellent training in clinical transplantation and basic science'; '34 peer-reviewed publications of which 11 were first authored.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals / Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the quality, clarity, and appropriateness of the proposed career development and training activities, and the plan for mentoring and monitoring candidate progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for didactic and laboratory training that fill identified gaps (e.g., transplant immunology, biostatistics, ethics), comprehensive monitoring and evaluation components, and specific elements like research ethics, lab management, and leadership. The summary notes when the applicant has revised the plan in response to prior critiques and includes letters indicating support for training (e.g., microsurgical models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific rationale, significance, innovation, rigor, preliminary data, experimental design, and feasibility of the proposed research aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether the area is clinically relevant and significant, conceptual innovation (e.g., expanding regulatory cells during NEVLP), robustness of preliminary data (sample sizes, flow cytometry gating), need for mechanistic studies, appropriateness and rigor of animal models, potential problems/alternative approaches, and specificity of proposed approaches (e.g., concerns about anti-PD-L1 not specifically targeting DCregs or lack of validation for OX-62 antibody). Strengths and weaknesses are listed (e.g., 'Physiological model of liver transplantation in rodent model'; weaknesses: 'Some approaches still lack specificity for DCregs').

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentors, Co-Mentors, Consultants, Collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the mentoring team composition, each member's expertise, mentoring experience, and how complementary their expertise is relative to the candidate's needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for an outstanding mentoring team of recognized experts with highly complementary areas of expertise and substantial mentoring experience. Example strengths: 'Outstanding mentoring team consisting of recognized experts' and named mentors with appropriate roles. Weaknesses are noted if mentoring is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment & Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the institutional environment, available resources, and documented institutional commitment (e.g., protected time, start-up support) that will support the candidate's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the institution provides an exceptional environment for development (research resources, staff, protected time). Example indicators: letters of support, 75% protected time guarantee, fully equipped and staffed laboratory, strong start-up package. Strengths are noted (e.g., 'Very strong institutional support'); weaknesses if lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness for Resubmissions (A1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is a resubmission, reviewers assess whether the applicant has adequately addressed prior critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee comments may state resubmission status (e.g., 'Resubmissions: Acceptable') and summarize how prior concerns were addressed (e.g., expanded preliminary data, revised career development plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to address human subjects protections where applicable; sufficiency is coded (e.g., NOT APPLICABLE (CODE 10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When human subjects are involved, reviewers evaluate protections; in this application code 10 indicates no human subjects involved. Guidance includes checking regulatory compliance and ethical safeguards when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of plans for the care and use of vertebrate animals in proposed studies and whether the protection of vertebrate animal welfare is adequately described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application: 'VERTEBRATE ANIMAL: ACCEPTABLE (CODE 30) — The protection of Vertebrate Animal welfare is adequately described.' Reviewers look for appropriate animal welfare protocols, justification of animal models, and adherence to standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard / Biosafety
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to prevent risks during handling of biohazard materials or samples, including biosafety level and facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers examine whether biosafety practices (e.g., BSL-2, biosafety cabinets) are described and adequate. This application: 'BIOHAZARD COMMENT: ACCEPTABLE' and notes 'BSL-2: Biosafety cabinets described.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the proposed RCR training plan and whether the required elements are adequately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five elements (format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, frequency) must be addressed. This application: 'TRAINING IN THE RESPONSIBLE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH: ACCEPTABLE — All 5 elements are adequately addressed.' Reviewers look for appropriate format, content, faculty involvement, and schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of whether select agent work is involved and appropriate compliance plans are provided (NOT APPLICABLE if none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If select agents are relevant, detailed compliance plans are required. In this application: 'SELECT AGENT: NOT APPLICABLE.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data, Model Organisms, Genomic Data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to include plans for sharing data, model organisms, and genomic data where applicable; codes indicate applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note applicability and adequacy. In this application: 'DATA SHARING PLAN: NOT APPLICABLE', 'MODEL ORGANISMS SHARING PLAN: NOT APPLICABLE', 'GENOMIC DATA SHARING PLAN: NOT APPLICABLE.' When applicable, specific sharing plans and commitments are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for authentication of critical biological and chemical materials used in the research to ensure reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether adequate plans are outlined to authenticate reagents, cell lines, antibodies, etc. This application: 'AUTHENTICATION OF KEY BIOLOGICAL AND/OR CHEMICAL RESOURCES: ACCEPTABLE — Adequate plans ... are outlined.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary Overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of whether there is a budgetary or scientific overlap with other active awards or resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If overlap exists, reviewers note conflicts; otherwise code as NOT APPLICABLE. This application: 'BUDGETARY OVERLAP: NOT APPLICABLE.' Committee also provided 'COMMITTEE BUDGET RECOMMENDATIONS: The budget is recommended as requested in all years.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Critique Practices / Content of Summary Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary statement contains reviewer critiques prepared by assigned reviewers and a RESUME AND SUMMARY OF DISCUSSION prepared by the Scientific Review Officer summarizing committee discussion; these explain how reviewer comments relate to the assigned overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRITIQUE section is provided without significant modification by staff to indicate the range of comments made during discussion and may not reflect the final outcome. The RESUME AND SUMMARY OF DISCUSSION summarizes the final committee opinion and is the basis for the assigned Overall Impact/Priority score. This guidance clarifies provenance of strengths/weaknesses and that criterion scores are collected prior to meeting.
